evidence.observation: Plan: "`api.judgments` drops `guard_path` and `guard_bytes` and loads the model with `load_model_bytes_composed(mr, source=model_path, root=model_path.parent)` ... References keep their binding through `bind_declared_references(model, root=reference_root or model_path.parent)`". In src/gnd/model/__init__.py:362-376, `_composed_view` runs `retained_root(root)` and then binds references whenever `model.reference_populations` is set (`model._references = _bind_at(model, descriptor)`). It raises ReferenceInputError (a ValueError, errors.py:174) if they cannot be bound under that root. `--reference-root` is a public option (commands/judgments.py:14). A model whose reference files live only under --reference-root therefore fails before line 1165 is reached. As the plan words it (every model), a model without includes would also regress, which breaks R0.6 and IR1-C7. Spec lines 93-100 limit the composed loader to roots that declare includes, but an include root with a reference population (the checking.orm.json fixture has one) plus a separate --reference-root still fails, and the spec says nothing about it.
"Every changed route gives byte-identical output for a model that declares no includes."

concerns.recommendation: In §2 IR1, say the composed loader is used only for roots that declare includes, as the spec does. Then either compose with a root that also holds the references, or state that --reference-root is refused or unsupported for include roots. Add a criterion or test that runs an include root with a reference population under a separate --reference-root.
concerns.title: IR1 composed loader binds references at the model directory and ignores --reference-root

evidence.observation: Plan: "`evaluate_judgments` drops its include guard. Its raw-subject check (`judgments.py:506-515`) re-derives the model ... Without `model_root` an include root keeps refusing". IR1-C6: "`test_R4_judgments` stays as the pin of the refusal". tests/test_mc1_guards.py:240-245 calls `evaluate_judgments(None, (), ...)` and expects ModelValidationError 'include:unsupported-route'. If the guard is dropped and the refusal moves into the raw-subject check at :507, the earlier policy shape check (`refuse()` at judgments.py:473-478) fires first with JudgmentInputError, and test_R4 fails. Spec line 125 actually keeps the guard as the first statement ("`if model_root is None: guard_bytes(...)`"), which contradicts the plan's "drops".

concerns.recommendation: Reword §2 IR1 to match the spec: the include guard stays as the first statement when model_root is None and is skipped only when model_root is given.
concerns.title: Plan says evaluate_judgments drops its guard, but IR1-C6 needs it kept first

evidence.observation: Plan cites "`error.reason: \"include:unsupported-route\"` (`api.py:1194-1197`)". In src/gnd/api.py, line 1194 is the closing `)` of the JudgmentInputError branch. The `except ModelValidationError` branch that writes `"reason": reason or "binding"` is at lines 1195-1198.

concerns.title: H6 cites api.py:1194-1197; the branch is at 1195-1198

evidence.observation: §5 says "each later phase adds its row" to the route list in representation-format.md and calls for "One entry per phase under the unreleased heading of `docs/release-notes.md`". In the §3 'Homes it changes' column, the IR3 row lists only `docs/agents/export-and-review.md` among docs, and no row lists `docs/release-notes.md`. H10 makes these homes the basis of the rule that milestones never write the same files at once.

concerns.recommendation: Add docs/release-notes.md to every phase's homes and the representation-format route list to IR3's homes.
concerns.title: §3 home lists omit docs that §5 assigns to each phase

summary: Plan r2 can be built and tested. Nearly all of its code citations match this checkout: api.py:1156-1163, judgments.py:470-471/507/569, emit.py:21/27-31/35-36/60-64, pyrel_rules.py:2415/357, _includes.py:217-218, extract/service.py:191, projection.py:319, and the named tests and lanes. The D4 receipt binding is sufficient: the receipt binds the root's sha256, the root pins each include, and compose refuses hash-mismatch, so the receipt binds every include. Four concerns remain. The IR1 loader call as written binds reference populations at the model directory, which ignores --reference-root. The plan's 'drops its include guard' wording contradicts IR1-C6. The H6 line range is off by one. The section 3 home lists leave out docs that section 5 assigns.
